ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, wooden blocks A and B, both of mass m, are connected by a light spring with stiffness coefficient k, and initially the system is at rest. A constant force of magnitude F=2mg and direction vertically upward is used to pull A until B just leaves the ground. What is the magnitude of the initial acceleration when A begins to rise?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The magnitude of A's initial acceleration upward is 2g
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the upper part is wooden block A, the lower part is wooden block B, and B is placed on the horizontal ground; a vertical light spring is connected between A and B. The problem states that the masses of the two wooden blocks are both m, the spring stiffness coefficient is k, the initial system is at rest, and later a vertically upward constant force F=2mg is applied to A. Then reason: when initially at rest, the forces on wooden block A are balanced. A is subjected to gravity mg downward, and the elastic force of the spring on A is upward, so the magnitude of the initial elastic force of the spring on A is mg. At the instant when the upward constant force is just applied and A just begins to rise, the deformation of the spring has not had time to change, so the elastic force of the spring on A is still mg and its direction is upward. Taking vertically upward as positive for A, according to Newton's second law: F+F_elastic-mg=ma, that is, 2mg+mg-mg=ma, so ma=2mg, giving a=2g.
